key_insight: Combining multiscale spatial learning, temporal modeling, and physics-based regularization improves reconstruction of time-resolved 3D turbulent flows from coarse-grained data.
engineering_relevance: The framework could recover useful fine-scale flow information when high-resolution simulation or measurement is too expensive.
method: Couple a multiscale neural operator with a state space model to reconstruct volumetric structures and maintain temporal consistency.
Use Navier–Stokes residuals as soft constraints to encourage physically plausible dynamics.
Apply a mixture-of-experts mechanism for unsupervised adaptation to unknown coarse-graining.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on canonical turbulent systems and atmospheric reanalysis data report lower reconstruction errors than learning-based and classical baselines, with better spatial and temporal coherence.
watch_item: Soft physics constraints do not guarantee physical consistency, and the abstract provides no quantitative error reductions or computational costs.
paper_title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics
